name: Body groomer (manscaping trimmer)

lead: A body groomer is a guarded electric trimmer designed for chest, abdomen, underarm and other body hair. People use it to keep hair short instead of fully shaving.
No clinical research on the devices themselves was found; the technology descends from electric hair clippers.

paras: Oscillating blades cut hair at a length set by an attachable guard, leaving a short stubble rather than a skin-level cut.

Evidence specific to the device is absent. Clinical sources on ingrown hairs note that very close shaving can provoke them in people with curly hair, and that trimming to a short length is a common alternative.

lead: A body groomer, often marketed as a manscaping trimmer, is an electric device with guarded blades intended to shorten or remove body hair on the chest, abdomen, underarms and other areas below the neck. It is a variant of the electric hair clipper and trimmer, which has been commercially available since the early 1920s.[1]

In looksmaxxing and grooming discussions it is mentioned as a way to keep body hair at a chosen short length rather than removing it completely. Published research specifically on body groomers is not available; the sources describing the underlying clipper technology focus on head and beard use.[1]
infobox: Electric clipper, first patented 1921 (Leo J. Wahl)

paras: Electric clippers are driven by a motor that oscillates the blades; motor designs include magnetic, rotary and pivot types, and attachable guards determine the length of hair left behind.[1] Body groomers apply this principle in a smaller, typically waterproof or rounded-blade format. Product details vary by manufacturer and are not covered in the encyclopedic sources consulted.

Manual clippers were reportedly invented around 1855 by the Serbian barber Nikola Bizumic, and Leo J. Wahl patented the first electric clipper in 1921, with Andis and Oster following in the same decade.[1] The dedicated body-hair variant is a later consumer product; no authoritative history of it was found.

Wikipedia notes that bodybuilders and some athletes shave or reduce body hair to highlight muscle definition, and some men also remove underarm hair.[2] Trimmers are one tool people use for this, as an alternative to razors.

No studies on body groomers were found. Research on razors indicates that close shaving can cause ingrown hairs in people with curly hair, and clinical advice for that condition often suggests keeping hair at a short but not skin-level length, for example with a trimmer on a low setting.[3]

timeline.event: Manual clippers reportedly invented by Nikola Bizumic.[1]
